In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, there is radial tear at the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, there is focal low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at the medial trochlea (about intact9* 1.2 cm). There is thin cord medial suprapatellar synovial plica. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. There is no tibial translation. 
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of left knee effusion with synovitis is present. There is thin cord medial suprapatellar synovial plica (about 1.7 mm thickness). The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.  Focal low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at the medial trochlea (about intact9* 1.2 cm), left knee.

There is a mild - moderate knee effusion. There is complex degenerate tearing and maceration of the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus with a horizontal tear seen along the posterior horn. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage. Normal lateral tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Complex degenerate tearing of the posterior body and horn of the medial meniscus. Mild - moderate knee effusion.

Descartar lesión LCA.

del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial.
Menisco medial de morfología conservada con alteración de señal del cuerno posterior que no
cumple criterios de rotura. Destaca leve edema en la interfase meniscocapsular del cuerno
posterior del menisco medial.
Rotura longitudinal vertical en la periferia del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral en sitio inserción
del ligamento menisco femoral de Wrisberg.
Alteración de señal e irregularidad superficial del cartílago femorotibial, sin defectos condrales
profundos.
Cartílago rotuliano con alteración de señal e irregularidad superficial en faceta lateral y medial.
Úlcera condral de espesor subtotal con componente delaminativo, sin cambios óseos reactivos en
vertiente medial, región central y vertiente lateral de la tróclea, se extiende 13 mm medio lateral y
10 mm craneocaudal.
Perdida de tensión del tendón rotuliano.
Restantes tendones regionales de espesor y señal conservados.
Acentuado derrame articular. No se observa quiste de Baker.
Edema del tejido celular subcutáneo y de los planos intermusculares.

Rotura completa del LCA con contusiones óseas en cóndilo femoral lateral y platillo tibial lateral,
sugerentes de evento de inestabilidad reciente.
Esguince grado I del componente superficial del LCM.
Edema la interfase meniscocapsular del cuerno posterior del menisco medial, pudiera traducir
lesión a este nivel.
Rotura vertical periférica del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral en sitio de inserción del
ligamento menisco femoral posterior (de Wrisberg).
Condropatía femorotibial superficial. Condropatía rotuliana superficial. Defecto condral grado 2-3 que compromete vertiente medial, región central y vertiente lateral de la
tróclea.
Acentuado derrame articular.

Findings:  Large knee joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments.  Complex degenerate tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a full-thickness radial component at the posterior horn. Minor mucoid degeneration of the body of the lateral meniscus which is otherwise intact.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band and popliteus tendon.  Minor insertional tendinosis and enthesopathy at the superior pole of the patella at the quadriceps tendon insertion.  Low-grade chondral thinning in the medial tibiofemoral compartment. Relatively well-maintained hyaline articular cartilage in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment. Low-grade chondral thinning along the trochlear groove. The patellofemoral hyaline articular cartilage is otherwise relatively well-maintained.  
Conclusion:  Complex degenerate tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a full-thickness radial component at the posterior horn. Large knee joint effusion.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Tendinopatía versus meniscopatía.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
LCA y ligamentos colaterales dentro de límites normales.
LCP con aumento de señal en su tercio medio que podría representar una lesión parcial
intrasustancia.
Rotura compleja del cuerno posterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco lateral con leve extrusión
meniscal.
Aumento de señal vertical periférica, incompleta del cuerno posterior del menisco medial que
podría representar una lesión al menos parcial regional.
Condropatía superficial de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial lateral. Cartílagos del
compartimento femorotibial medial y patelofemoral sin alteraciones.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Discreto edema de las partes blandas entre la banda de tibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Impresión:
Rotura compleja del cuerno posterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco lateral con leve extrusión
meniscal.
Signos de rotura compleja del cuerno posterior del menisco medial.
Condropatía superficial de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Aumento de señal del tercio medio del LCP, sin poder descartar una lesión parcial regional.

MRI RIGHT KNEE

Clinical information: [Age]. Ongoing medial meniscus pain with mechanical symptoms and swelling.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the right knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Comparison examination: Previous radiographs of bilateral knees from [Date].

FINDINGS:
There is a radial tear involving the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus measuring 0.8 cm. There are extensive degenerative changes of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus with extensive apical fraying. There is a focal oblique tear involving the posterior horn and posterior aspect of the body of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface.

There is a chronic tearing of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is a T2 hyperintensity within the midportion of the posterior cruciate ligament measuring 0.4 x 0.3 cm representing a small intraligamentous ganglion.

There is mild thickening of the proximal medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. The extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There is a focal severe chondrosis involving the weightbearing zone and posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle with focal deep cartilage defect and small adjacent cystic changes. There are no deep cartilage defects in the medial femorotibial joint compartment. There is a mild superficial chondral disease involving the patellofemoral joint. There are focal small osteophytes at the inner aspect of the intercondylar notch

There is a mild anterior tibial translation [9 mm]. The no acute bony contusions. There is a mild joint effusion with reactive synovial thickening. There are multiple intra-articular bodies, for example posterior to the distal attachment of the posterior cruciate ligament measuring 0.6 x 0.4 cm. There is a large (2.0 x 0.8 cm), well-corticated bone fragment adjacent to the posterolateral aspect of the tibial plateau, representing another intra-articular body.

There is a low volume Baker's cyst. Small cluster of cysts in the popliteal fossa measuring a maximum of 10 mm AP by 20 mm transverse radiology a of a of alcohol

The visualized muscle bulk is unremarkable.

Conclusion:
1. Degenerative radial tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Underlying severe degenerative changes of the lateral meniscus with apical fraying.
2. Oblique tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface.
3. Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. No acute bony contusions.
4. Moderate femorotibial osteoarthritis with severe chondrosis in the lateral femorotibial joint compartment as described in detail above.
5. Mild joint effusion with intra-articular bodies.
